cite: PLAN.md §3.5 sourced cutting data; saw_cut row sfm = blade linear speed, feed_mm_min = descent feed
inventory machine blade_speed_sfm [min, max], inclusive clamp

example (plausible, not measured); Machinery's Handbook 27th ed. (Industrial Press, 2004) p.1142 bimetal band-saw speed for 1018, 300 fpm (4 in material, 3/4 variable-tooth blade, cutting fluid); +10% for the about 1.4 in average length of cut through the 1-3/4 in bar (+10% at 1-1/4 in) = 330 fpm, then -30% to -50% for cutting dry = 165-231 fpm; 200 fpm is inside that range and is the 4x6 saw's top belt step (Harbor Freight item 93762 manual p.10 Fig. H, 80/120/200 FPM). Blade: p.1138 tooth selection chart, solid round 1-3/4 in (44.45 mm) length of cut = 4/6 variable pitch. Feed: p.1140 cutting-rate graph, 4/6 line at 200 fpm about 4.8 sq in/min (p.1142's worked example reads the same 4/6 line at about 4 sq in/min at 130 fpm); 65 mm/min (2.56 in/min) descent across the full 1.75 in width removes at most 4.5 sq in/min (about 3.5 average over the round), at the graph's starting rate, which p.1140 says to adjust from the chips
findings.message: Blade speed is sourced from the saw_cut row and clamped to the machine's blade-speed range; the work is fed by hand, sawn on the waste side of the scribed line.
